questions.question: For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D) $\min\{\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\colon\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c},\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$, which conditions on feasible $\boldsymbol{x}$, $\boldsymbol{y}$ hold exactly when both are optimal?
options: $(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y})_j=c_j$ for all $j$ and $(\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x})_i=b_i$ for all $i$

$\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$, together with $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c}$
$x_j(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c})_j=0$ for all $j$ and $y_i(\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x})_i=0$ for all $i$
exactly one of $x_j$ and $(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c})_j$ is zero for each $j$, and likewise for each $i$

questions.question: For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D), let $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast},\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$ be optimal with $(\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast})_2<b_2$. What does complementary slackness give?
options: $(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast})_2=c_2$

questions.question: In the resource-buyer reading of (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual, $c_j$ is the unit profit of product $j$, $a_{ij}$ its use of resource $i$ and $y_i$ the unit price of resource $i$. If optimal $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast},\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$ have $x_j^{\ast}>0$, which relation holds?
options: $\sum_ia_{ij}y_i^{\ast}>c_j$: the resources for one unit are worth more than its profit
$\sum_ia_{ij}y_i^{\ast}<c_j$: making one unit earns more than selling its resources
$\sum_ib_iy_i^{\ast}=c_j$: the value of all resources equals the profit of one unit
$\sum_ia_{ij}y_i^{\ast}=c_j$: the resources for one unit are worth exactly its profit

questions.question: For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D), let $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast},\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$ be optimal with constraint 1 of (P) binding, $(\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast})_1=b_1$. What does complementary slackness say about $y_1^{\ast}$?
options: $y_1^{\ast}>0$, since a binding constraint is a bottleneck.
Nothing beyond $y_1^{\ast}\geq0$: it can be positive or zero.
$y_1^{\ast}=0$, since the slack of constraint 1 is zero.
$y_1^{\ast}>0$ whenever all entries of $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ are positive.

questions.question: For $\max 4x_1+3x_2+5x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+2x_3\leq5$, $x_1+2x_2+x_3\leq9$, $2x_1+x_2+3x_3\leq8$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}=(2,0,1)$ is optimal, with $y_i$ belonging to constraint $i$. Which primal variables does complementary slackness force to be zero in every optimal $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$?
options: Only $x_2^{\ast}$, since its partner dual variable $y_2^{\ast}$ is zero.
Only $x_3^{\ast}$, since dual constraint 3 has surplus $7-5=2$.
$x_1^{\ast}$ and $x_2^{\ast}$, since dual constraints 1 and 2 are tight.
None; complementary slackness forces zeros only among the $y_i$.

questions.question: For $\max 5x_1+6x_2$ subject to $3x_2\leq12$, $x_1+2x_2\leq10$, $x_1\leq9$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}=(0,3,2)$ is optimal, with $y_i$ belonging to constraint $i$. Which primal constraints must be binding at every optimal $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$?
options: Only constraint 1, since $y_1^{\ast}=0$ marks a binding constraint.
Constraints 1 and 2, since dual constraints 1 and 2 are tight.
None; the conditions only lead from $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ to $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$.
Constraints 2 and 3, since $y_2^{\ast}$ and $y_3^{\ast}$ are positive.

questions.question: For $\max 4x_1+3x_2$ subject to $2x_1+x_2\leq8$, $x_1+2x_2\leq7$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, and its dual $\min 8y_1+7y_2$ subject to $2y_1+y_2\geq4$, $y_1+2y_2\geq3$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, take the feasible pair $\boldsymbol{x}=(2,1)$, $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2)$. What is the duality gap $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$?

For $\max 3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $x_1+3x_2\leq6$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with dual constraints $y_1+y_2\geq3$, $y_1+3y_2\geq2$, $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the pair $\boldsymbol{x}=(3,1)$, $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,0)$ is feasible. Which complementary slackness condition fails?
options: $y_2(6-x_1-3x_2)=0$ fails, as $y_2=0$ at a binding constraint.
$y_1(4-x_1-x_2)=0$ fails, as $y_1=3$ is positive.
$x_2(y_1+3y_2-2)=0$ fails: it equals $1\cdot1=1$.
$x_1(y_1+y_2-3)=0$ is violated by the positive value $x_1=3$.

questions.question: For $\max 5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\leq10$, $3x_1+x_2\leq9$, $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the point $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}=(2,3)$ is feasible. Which system does complementary slackness give for the dual variables $y_1,y_2,y_3$ of the three constraints?

For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D), a feasible $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ and a $\boldsymbol{y}$ with $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c}$ but $y_1<0$ satisfy all complementary slackness products. What does $\boldsymbol{y}$ show about $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$?
options: Nothing: $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$, but with $y_1<0$ weak duality does not apply.
$\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ is optimal, as the products vanish and $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{c}$ holds.
$\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ is not optimal, as $y_1<0$ pushes $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ below $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$.
$\boldsymbol{y}$ is optimal for (D), since its value equals $\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$.

questions.question: For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D), feasible $\boldsymbol{x}$, $\boldsymbol{y}$ have $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}^{\top}(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c})+\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}(\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x})$. Why is this gap zero exactly when every term is zero?
options: By strong duality the gap is zero for every feasible pair, so each of the products must be zero as well.
The identity holds only for optimal pairs, and for those every product is zero by the definition of optimality.
Feasibility makes each product a product of two nonnegative numbers, and nonnegative terms sum to zero only if each is zero.
Each product is at most zero, because $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$ makes every entry $(\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x})_i\leq0$.

questions.question: For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D), (P) has optimal solutions $\boldsymbol{x}'\neq\boldsymbol{x}''$, and an optimal $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$ of (D) was found from $\boldsymbol{x}'$ by complementary slackness. Do $\boldsymbol{x}''$, $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$ satisfy the conditions?
options: Not necessarily: they hold only for the solution used to compute $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$.
Yes: $\boldsymbol{x}''$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}$ form an optimal pair, so every product vanishes.
Only if $\boldsymbol{x}''$ is a corner point of the feasible region of (P).
Only if $\boldsymbol{x}'$ and $\boldsymbol{x}''$ are positive in the same coordinates.

questions.question: For $\max 5x_1+2x_2+3x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\leq10$, $2x_1+3x_2+x_3\leq12$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with dual variables $y_1,y_2$ for the two constraints, test $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}=(2,0,8)$ for optimality with complementary slackness. Which verdict, with its reason, is correct?
options: Not optimal: dual constraint 2 gives $7>2$, but it should hold with equality.
Not optimal: the conditions give $y_2=-2<0$, so no dual feasible $\boldsymbol{y}$ fits.
Optimal: both constraints bind, and a feasible point binding every constraint is optimal.
Optimal: $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2)$ is dual feasible, and both values are $34$.

questions.question: For $\max 5x_1+6x_2$ subject to $3x_1+2x_2\leq8$, $2x_1+2x_2\leq6$, $2x_1+x_2\leq12$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with dual variables $y_1,y_2,y_3$, test the feasible point $\boldsymbol{x}=(2,1)$ for optimality with complementary slackness. What do you conclude?
options: Optimal: $\boldsymbol{y}=(-1,4,0)$ meets the conditions, and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=16=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$.
Not optimal: the conditions force $\boldsymbol{y}=(-1,4,0)$, which is not dual feasible.
Optimal: the conditions give $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,\tfrac{3}{2},0)$, which is nonnegative, so it is dual feasible.
Undecided: another solution of the conditions with $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ might still exist.

questions.question: For $\max 3x_1+5x_2+6x_3$ subject to $x_1+3x_2+x_3\leq4$, $x_1+4x_2+3x_3\leq8$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the dual solution $\boldsymbol{y}^{\ast}=(\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{3}{2})$ is optimal. Which point does complementary slackness give as the optimal primal solution?

For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D) and a feasible $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$, the system $y_i=0$ for each constraint $i$ with slack and $(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y})_j=c_j$ for each $j$ with $x_j^{\ast}>0$ has no solution. What can be concluded?
options: (P) is unbounded, since no dual price vector can fit the candidate $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$.
Nothing, as the conditions only certify optimality when a dual feasible solution exists.
$\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ is not optimal, though (P) may still have an optimal solution elsewhere.
(D) is infeasible, since no $\boldsymbol{y}$ at all satisfies the conditions with $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$.

questions.question: For (P) $\max\{\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ and its dual (D), complementary slackness is proved by writing the gap $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ as a sum of the product terms. Which direction of the proof needs strong duality, not only weak duality?
options: Conditions $\Rightarrow$ optimal pair: a zero gap alone cannot exclude a better feasible $\boldsymbol{x}$.
Both directions, since weak duality says nothing about feasible pairs whose gap is zero.
Neither: the gap identity on its own shows that optimal pairs are those with zero gap.
Optimal pair $\Rightarrow$ conditions: one needs the equality of the optimal values of (P) and (D).

questions.question: For $\max 3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $x_1\leq2$, $x_2\leq2$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, a student tests $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}=(2,2)$: all constraints bind, the conditions give $y_1+y_2=3$ and $y_1+y_3=2$, and choosing $y_2=0$ yields $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,0,-1)$. What is the correct conclusion?
options: $\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ is not optimal, since the conditions led to $y_3=-1<0$.
$\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ is optimal: $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2,1)$ also meets the conditions and is dual feasible.
$\boldsymbol{x}^{\ast}$ is optimal, and $\boldsymbol{y}=(3,0,-1)$ is an optimal dual solution.
No conclusion: at a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$ with three binding constraints the test fails.

questions.question: For $\max 4x_1+4x_2+3x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\leq7$, $3x_1+x_2+x_3\leq9$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the feasible $\boldsymbol{x}=(1,0,6)$ binds both constraints, and the conditions for $x_1,x_3>0$ give $\boldsymbol{y}=(\tfrac{5}{2},\tfrac{1}{2})$. Which check settles whether $\boldsymbol{x}$ is optimal, and how?
options: Dual constraint 2: $y_1+y_2=3<4$ fails, so $\boldsymbol{x}$ is not optimal.
The sign check $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$: it passes, so $\boldsymbol{x}$ is optimal.
The values: $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=22=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$, so $\boldsymbol{x}$ is optimal.
The slacks: both are zero, so $\boldsymbol{y}$ must be $\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}$ is not optimal.
